gloss: making the bench; being selected for the game-day roster

definitions.gloss: making the bench; being selected for the game-day roster
definitions.explanation: Being included in the group of players who sit on the bench during a game, meaning they are eligible to play as substitutes. Used primarily in baseball and other team sports in Japan.

examples.japanese: やっとベンチ{入|い}りできた。
ベンチ{入|い}りメンバーが{発表|はっぴょう}された。
ケガから{復帰|ふっき}して{久|ひさ}しぶりにベンチ{入|い}りを{果|は}たした{選手|せんしゅ}は、{涙|なみだ}を{見|み}せた。
examples.english: The player who returned from injury and made the bench for the first time in a while showed tears.

notes:
A compound of ベンチ (bench) + {入|い}り (entering, being included). In Japanese sports, especially {野球|やきゅう} (baseball) and サッカー (soccer), ベンチ{入|い}り means being selected to the active roster for a game. It does not necessarily mean the player will play -- they may remain on the bench as a substitute.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ベンチ{入|い}りする: to make the bench (verb form)
- ベンチ{入|い}りメンバー: bench roster members
- ベンチ{入|い}りを{果|は}たす: to achieve bench selection
- ベンチ{入|い}りを{逃|のが}す: to miss bench selection

CONTRASTED WITH:
- スタメン / {先発|せんぱつ}メンバー: starting lineup -- players who start the game
- ベンチ{外|がい}: not on the bench -- not selected for the game-day roster at all
- {控|ひか}え{選手|せんしゅ}: reserve player, substitute

USAGE:
For young or recovering players, ベンチ{入|い}り itself is an achievement and milestone, even if they do not get playing time.
